messages.subject: semTools::reliability vs psych::alpha
parts:
Results of the coefficients alpha calculated with semTools::reliability after running a CFA are very different from those calculated with aggregated measures using psych::alpha.

In one case we are considering latent variables and observed in the other, however can someone explain me better how semTools calculate reliability and the motivation behind such difference?  I tried to have a look of the different formulas from the pdf packages but I'm still confused.

Thanks,

Fran

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: semTools::reliability vs psych::alpha
parts: can someone explain me better how semTools calculate reliability and the motivation behind such difference?

The formulas aren't the difference.  As the help-page states, semTools::reliability() calculates alpha using polychoric correlations (so it is the lower-bound of reliability of the latent item responses), whereas I'm certain psych::alpha() simply treats the ordinal variables as continuous.  This comparative article might verify that:

https://doi.apa.org/doi/10.1037/met0000144

You can try passing the estimated polychoric correlation matrix from your lavaan model to  psych::alpha() to see if the results then match semTools::reliability().  Using the example from the ?lavTables help page, they match for me:

example(lavTables)
EstPoly <- lavInspect(fit, "sampstat")$cov
psych::alpha(EstPoly) # for 9 all variables
## compare to the last column:
semTools::reliability(fit, return.total = TRUE)
